findings.title: Null credentialIds from delegation credentials break the connectedCalendars query
findings.body: `connectedCalendars.map((cal) => cal.credentialId)` collects credential IDs and passes them straight into `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`, which runs `prisma.calendarCache.groupBy({ where: { credentialId: { in: credentialIds } } })`. For delegation credentials, connected calendar entries have `credentialId: null` (they are identified by `delegationCredentialId` instead — the UI in this same PR handles that case). Passing `null` inside the `in` array for the non-nullable Int field `credentialId` causes a PrismaClientValidationError, so the entire `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` query fails for any user who has a delegation-credential calendar connection. The IDs should be filtered (e.g. `.filter((id): id is number => typeof id === 'number')`) before querying.

findings.title: Cache deletion does not invalidate connectedCalendars, leaving stale cache status in the UI
findings.body: The `deleteCacheMutation` only calls `showToast` and the optional `onSuccess` prop on success, but unlike the `disconnectMutation` in the same file it never invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. After the user deletes the cache, the dropdown continues to show the old "Last updated" timestamp and keeps offering "Delete cached data" until a full refetch happens (and the query is configured with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` in the wrapper). Add `await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` (as done for the disconnect mutation) so the cache status disappears immediately after deletion.

findings.title: Script uses macOS-only sed syntax and fails on Linux
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is the BSD/macOS form of in-place sed; on GNU/Linux `sed -i ''` treats the empty string as a file name and the script errors out. Since this helper script is committed for the whole team, developers on Linux cannot use it to update GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL. Use a portable form (e.g. `sed -i.bak -E ... && rm file.bak`) or detect the platform. Additionally, `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the caller's working directory, so running the script from anywhere other than its own directory silently creates/edits the wrong .env file.
